doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Buddy Rich, Alvino Rey and Manhattan School
title: Not remembering his own arrangements
summary: Mandel says he often forgets what he wrote until he hears it played back, which feels as if he dreamt it.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So what else did you write for him?

I don’t know, I wrote a lot of things… I wrote some originals, I can’t remember a lot of the stuff I wrote. You know people mention them to me and it sort of comes back and I wonder if I wrote it or dreamt it. The strangest experience, maybe you’ve heard this from guys like Ralph Burns, is when you send an arrangement in and you never hear it played live… if you hear it played back years later, it’s the most eerie feeling in the world because you’re not sure if you wrote it or you dreamt it.

Very strange, it’s like a totally incomplete feeling ‘cause usually you write something and after I’ve written something I totally forget how it goes, until I hear it played back again at rehearsal, then it all comes back like boom. Even today when I record, I walk in the studio, I can’t remember what I wrote but I have instant recall the minute I hear it played back, so if I don’t hear it played back… For years, I used to send a lot of things out with acts, I’d send them out to bands when I stayed in New York, when I stayed here. I’d hear it back and it’s a very strange feeling.
